chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abu Hammam Isma'il ibn Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ghazwan, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Pray over the martyred (slain) from my nation, and over the one who kills himself from my nation; do not leave any from my nation without prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying over a martyr or one who committed suicide in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia scholarly view that the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit) is a communal obligation (or highly recommended) extended broadly to the Ummah, including martyrs and those who took their own lives. It underscores the inclusivity of the Prophet's mercy, ensuring no member is left without this spiritual honor, reflecting the tradition's emphasis on the intercessory power of the Prophet's supplications for all believers.
